newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian cotton prices rise on overseas buying.
newsitem.headline: Indian cotton prices rise on overseas buying.

text.p: Indian cotton prices rose on Thursday on overseas buying as well as lower arrivals, dealers said. Mill buying however remained low.
"New crop arrivals remained lower than expected due to severe cold weather at producing centres but are expected to pick up as soon as the weather improves," one broker said.

In spot deals Bengal-deshi rose by 20 rupees at 840/865 rupees per maund (37.32 kg) while Punjab saw-ginned gained by 10 rupees at 1,410/1,640 rupees. Gujarat Sankar-4 (long-staple) rose by 300/500 rupees to 17,000/17,500 rupees per candy (355.56 kg) for average variety and 18,500/19,000 for the superior type.
